description: Generate a Kotlin Multiplatform (Android + iOS) project's unit-test line/branch coverage with the Kover Gradle plugin (`org.jetbrains.kotlinx.kover`) — the root-aggregated `./gradlew koverXmlReport` (`build/reports/kover/report.xml`, covering every module listed in the root `dependencies { kover(project(":x")) }`) when the root aggregates, else each module's own report (`:<kmp-module>:koverXmlReport` → `<module>/build/reports/kover/report.xml`, or the Android-only `koverXmlReportAndroid` → `reportAndroid.xml`; an Android app module's `koverXmlReportDebug` → `reportDebug.xml`) — then parses the JaCoCo-format XML into exact totals, per-module and per-class line/branch percentages (each class mapped back to its module and source set — `commonMain`, `androidMain`, the app's `main`), and uncovered line numbers for classes under the bar. Coverage comes from the JVM test runs only (Android host tests, `jvmTest`, the Android app's `testDebugUnitTest`, which Kover runs itself): Kotlin/Native has no coverage tool, so `iosMain`/`appleMain`/`nativeMain` code is listed as "not measurable" and never fails the gate, and `commonMain` code is measured through the JVM targets' runs of `commonTest`. Invoke as `/iru-kmp-coverage [scope]`, where `[scope]` is one or more comma-separated class simple names, source paths, or a module (`:shared`), or with no argument for the whole project; optional `key: value` lines: `tests: <pattern>` to narrow the test run (the same `--tests` syntax as `iru-kmp-test`), `bar: <percent>` (default 80), `module:`, and `ios-app: yes` to also collect informational Xcode coverage of the SwiftUI host app's Swift code (`xcodebuild test -enableCodeCoverage YES` + `xccov`, behind the shared `.integration-test.lock`). Detects whether Kover is applied before running anything and reports "coverage not wired" (naming what's missing) instead of a false 0%/100% or a clean pass. Report-only: never adds tests or changes build files. Equivalent to `iru-android-coverage`/`iru-java-coverage`'s Kover path for KMP apps. Use whenever the user (or `iru-kmp-code-one-task-group` via `iru-gate-runner`) wants to check, or verify a bar (e.g. "at least 80% line coverage") for, KMP classes or modules.
